title: 12 V power
step: Connect a +12 V power adapter to the JPWR 2.10 mm barrel jack.
look_for: The barrel power jack marked JPWR and the Type-C to barrel plug adapter.

title: Debug serial console
step: Connect the debug UART micro-USB port to your host and open the second serial device, normally /dev/ttyUSB1, at 115200 baud.
look_for: The debug UART micro-USB port; the host exposes four serial devices and the second is the Main Domain console.

title: USB0 flashing
step: Connect the USB0 Type-C port to the host computer for software flashing.

title: USB1 host peripherals
step: Use the USB1 Type-C host-mode port for a USB peripheral.

title: DisplayPort outputs
step: Connect a monitor to DisplayPort0 (JEDP0) or JEDP1 using the supplied active Mini DisplayPort-to-DisplayPort cable.
look_for: The mini-DisplayPort outputs identified as JEDP0 and JEDP1.

title: Ethernet
step: Connect an Ethernet cable to an RJ45 Ethernet connector.
look_for: The RJ45 Ethernet connectors on the board.

title: Camera DIP switches
step: Check that SW1-5 through SW1-8 are OFF for CSI0 through CSI3 routed to the mainboard camera connectors.
look_for: The SW1 DIP switch bank with positions 5 through 8; ON routes those cameras to the GMSL mezzanine.

title: Speaker connections
step: Connect the two supplied mini speakers to the onboard speaker connections driven by the MAX98357 I2S amplifiers.
look_for: The two supplied mini speakers and their mainboard speaker connections.

title: Onboard microphone
step: Locate the single onboard MMICT5848 microphone on HS2_MI2S, configured to the left channel by default.
look_for: The single onboard microphone shown in the Audio documentation's microphone-location image.

title: Cooling fan
step: Locate the bottom-mounted CPU cooler and its fan connection at JFAN on the mainboard.
look_for: The fan-based cooler mounted to the bottom of the device and the JFAN connector.

title: Wi-Fi hardware
step: Locate the NFA765A Wi-Fi module in its M.2 slot and the ANT0 and ANT1 antenna connections.
look_for: The M.2 Wi-Fi module and its two antenna connections.
